messages.author: 5f1957cb9553c863
messages.subject: Identifying points on PCA graph
parts:
Hi!

I am still getting used to R so forgive me if there is an easy solution. I have one specimen that is skewing my results on my PCA graph so want to find a way to identify what specimen it is so that I can resolve this. 
Here is my code:

library(geomorph)
mydata <- readland.tps("Flipper ratios NEW.TPS", specID = "ID")
classifier <- read.csv("classifier flipper ratios.csv", header = TRUE)
is.factor(classifier$Morphotype)
coords <- as.matrix(mydata)
flipperratios.gpa <- gpagen(mydata, print.progress = FALSE)
summary(flipperratios.gpa)
plotAllSpecimens(flipperratios.gpa$coords, mean = TRUE, links = NULL, label = TRUE, plot.param = list())
flipperratios.pca <-plotTangentSpace(flipperratios.gpa$coords, axis1 = 1, axis2 = 2, groups = classifier$Morphotype, legend = TRUE)

Hope you can help, thanks in advance!

messages.author: baf6eb7bae06984d
messages.subject: Re: Identifying points on PCA graph
parts:
Dear Laura,

In your particular your outlier is has the maximum value along PC1, so convenient R function for that would be
which.max(flipperratios.pca$pcscores$PC1) (or whatever the vector holding the PC1 scores)

You can also use identify() function to get the actual value of a point you click on the graph

alternatively you can try to plot the labels of the specimens on top of PC values.

For a more general solution, where you want to be able to scroll over any point in a plot and see its identifier, have a look at qtlcharts.

The plots here include several nice examples: https://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/do_diagnostics.html

Here's a link to the package page: https://kbroman.org/qtlcharts/

And here's some very simple example code (assumed you've successfully installed all packages)
library(qtlcharts)
mymax <- 100
x <- 1:mymax
y <- sqrt(1:mymax)
labs <- paste0("ID", 1:mymax)
iplot(x, y, indID=labs,
      chartOpts=list(xlab="Integer", ylab="Sqrt"))

David

I typed that command as sort of representative syntax, I didn't meant it to be something you can get a result directly, as I wasn't sure whether individual pcs were stored as named list items  or data matrix on top of my head.

You need to provide the proper variable (PC1) from the plotTangentSpace() function.

I suggest looking up 
flipperratios.pca$pc.scores (which looks like returns an array)

That's a good way to learn more about R (and geomorph) and how data objects are stored and accessed.
